title: Sparsity under restriction and reindexing
statement: Let $n,k$ be natural numbers, let $p$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, let $J$ be a set of coordinates, let $z$ assign a sign to each coordinate outside $J$, and let $e$ be a bijection from the $k$ coordinates to $J$. The number of nonzero Fourier coefficients of the restriction of $p$ obtained by fixing the coordinates outside $J$ to $z$ and reindexing the remaining coordinates by $e$ is at most the number of nonzero Fourier coefficients of $p$.
hypotheses_covered: A real-valued function on the n-dimensional sign cube
A finite coordinate set J within the n coordinates
A fixed sign assignment on coordinates outside J
A bijection from the k coordinates to J
